en: **Title:** *Viśeṣastava* **Author:** Rādhasvāmin (also known as Bhaṭṭarādhasvāmin) **Source:** Schneider, Johannes. 2023. *Viśeṣastava*. Der Sanskrittext nach den Handschriften bearbeitet und übersetzt. Indica et Tibetica 61. Marburg: Indica et Tibetica Verlag. [Bilingual Sanskrit-Tibetan edition on pp. 54–85]
Homage to the Buddha!
Having completely set aside other teachers, I have gone for refuge to you.
Blessed One, what is the reason for this? You are faultless and possessed of all virtues. (1)
Either the world is devoted to faults, or it perceives faults as virtues, or it is dull in grasping virtues—therefore it has gone for refuge to others. || 2 ||
Those qualities which are proclaimed with joy by people through their devotion to Vāsudeva, Īśvara, and others, are in fact defects in your teaching. (3)
It is said that Tripura was burnt by Rudra with a single arrow in his wrath;
yet it was the fire of his anger itself that was consumed by you with the great arrow of knowledge.
For Hara was drawn back again by Kāma, who had been poorly burnt;
yet now, Kāma has been offered as an oblation into the fire of your wisdom and has gone to destruction along with his very roots. || 5 ||
The wielder of the trident became four-faced through his passion for Tilottamā;
yet, by the amorous charms of Māra’s daughters, not even a single hair on your body was stirred.
Even Śaṅkara, who carries a woman on half his body, surpasses the cakravāka birds; yet you are not deluded by desire at all, which is itself devoid of peace.
Neither the wielder of the discus nor the wielder of the trident is able to conquer that power of Māra;
yet you have conquered it by means of the weapon of loving-kindness, without the need for a discus or a trident.
Śarva was rendered blue-throated by the arrows of Jaras, and Hari was struck down by Bāṇa;
yet those two gods were subject to external causes, whereas you, O Lord, are free from such causes.
By assuming the form of a dwarf, Hari deceived Bali through his power of illusion;
you, however, being a knower of illusion, do not deceive others.
By them, Viṣṇu’s leaping across the three worlds was seen like the gait of a cripple;
yet by those who have not lost their sight of you, O Lord, the manifestation of your power has been seen as a marvel.
Even though the prince practiced celibacy along with his sixty thousand companions,
you reduced those seven who engaged in sexual union to ashes.
"For we are indeed the creators of the world," so it was said by Brahmā and the others;
yet you, the seer of truth, have stated that they and the world are born of karma. (13)
It is said that the wielder of the thunderbolt was indeed deluded by passion upon seeing Ahalyā;
yet you, O Hero, have abandoned your wife while being deluded by passion itself. (14)
Soma helplessly becomes a morsel for the elephant Rāhu;
there is no being whose power you do not helplessly come under.
Kings such as Rāma and Ambarīṣa returned once more from the forests;
but you, O Sugata, satisfied by the nectar of discernment, have not returned again.
"Those desiring to conquer heaven say that animals are to be sacrificed in the ritual;
yet, O sinless one, even the killing of an ant has not been permitted by you. (17)
In other sacrifices, others have offered their own lives as oblations for their own sake;
but by you alone has the offering of your own life been made for the sake of others.
Many people have been consumed by the sages when they were enraged by the fires of their curses;
but by you, the causes of rebirth for all people have been consumed by the fire of knowledge.
The ascetic success of the sages is inferred from their power of cursing;
O Lord, your ascetic success is inferred from your power of compassion. (20)
The *liṅga* of Śambhu was cast down by the sages through a curse because he was lustful; by you, however, Kāma himself—the very root of all misfortunes—has been struck down. (21)

O Sage, because of the vastness [of the subject] and the weakness of memory, the words of Vyāsa are heard everywhere as being contradictory in their earlier and later parts; yet such is not the case for you.
Generally, those doctrines which were spoken by Dvaipāyana and others have been uttered by you after you yourself realized the unique Dharma and made it manifest. (22)
The Vedas and the words of the heretics are spoken only in secluded places;
but your Dharma is proclaimed by the lion’s roar.
O Lord, although Bhāradvāja had realized the truth according to the Sāṃkhya system, he associated with Vasantī; your disciples, however, never associate with women at all.
"Gifts should be given only to the distinguished," thus said Ulūka;
"O Lord, you have declared that out of compassion, gifts should be given even to dogs. (25)
The Nirgranthas seek the destruction of their knots through physical austerities;
you, however, seek the destruction of your knots through mental austerities.
Logicians desire the establishment of entities while disregarding [causes];
yet it has been stated by you, O Vācaspati, that nothing exists without depending [on something else]. (27)
They say that Śuka indeed attained liberation after piercing through the solar disc;
you, however, have reached nirvāṇa, yet you have not gone anywhere at all.
Janaka attained liberation by one path, and Śuka went by another;
but your disciples have gone by that very same path by which you yourself have traveled.
Viṣṇu had sixteen thousand wives as his consorts;
you, however, are the supreme teacher of the world, free from possessiveness and without any belongings.
Vyāsa became transformed by his infatuation with Kāśīsundarī;
yet, even while living as a householder, you have not been deluded by ignoble sensory objects.
Vyāsa was overcome by desire and became distraught when struck by a woman’s foot; you, however, though living as a householder, were not shaken. (32)
It is said that Rāma went to the far shore of the great ocean seeking a woman;
you, however, have gone to the hermitage abandoning sixty thousand women. (33)
The slaying of Karṇa, Duryodhana, and the others was intended by Hari;
yet you have even surrendered your own life out of a desire for the welfare of all beings. (34)
That earth which was seized by Viṣṇu through deceit by means of his three strides,
has been abandoned by you, who seek liberation, as if it were a blade of grass.
The fame that Rāma attained by making the world devoid of Kṣatriyas with arrows that brought about the destruction of lives— that very thing is your infamy in the scriptures.
For whose sake the battle was waged by the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas—
you have departed, abandoning that royal fortune like a creeper infested with serpents.
Whatever was performed by the Lord of Yoga in the Devadāru forest of Śambhu was an act of ignorance once he had received your command. (38)
Even today, Indra is still sung of by the twice-born as the paramour of Ahalyā;
yet by your attainment of the first fruit, the fame of Śakra has been proclaimed.
For Kṛṣṇa, distressed by fear of the black Yavana, entered beneath the bed of Mucukunda; you, O Lord, are fearless in every respect. 40.
"O Sage, even for your disciples, your celibacy has been stainless; such was the report that Prajāpati desired his own daughter. (41)
"The transition [of the sun] is said to be like the receiving of a gift regarding merit and demerit;
for you have stated that this would result in the loss of what was done and the acquisition of what was not done. (42)
The Sāṃkhyas postulate that the self has volition as its characteristic;
if this were so, you have stated that the self is impermanent. (43)
Kaṇāda has proclaimed that the self is all-pervading and distinct from cognition;
yet, as you have stated, it follows that such a self would be ignorant and equivalent to a piece of wood. (44)
The individual soul (jīva) is both contracting and expanding, possessing the size of the body;
Nagna declared this because of its localized nature, and thus its perishability was stated by you.
The twice-born postulate that the Puruṣa is the eternal cause of the world;
yet you have stated that there is nothing which is both eternal and a cause. (46)
Even there, Kapila consumed the sixty thousand sons of the high-souled Sagara with his mere glance; yet even in that, you felt compassion.
Kapila, the knower of reality, declared that the world was produced from Pradhāna;
yet you have stated that the birth of the world arises from karma and afflictions. (48)
Even in their liberation, those such as Kapila regard the self as a cause for rebirth;
you, however, having attained peace, do not admit it into your reckoning, like a fire that has been extinguished.
By some founders of schools, liberation was declared to possess motion;
yet you, having understood that wherever there is motion there is cyclic existence, have revealed [the truth]. (50)
O Omniscient One, those very undertakings such as the construction of gardens—which are causes of sin for the naked ones—were indeed declared by you to be causes of merit. (51)
In the battle, the life-force (jīva) of Śiśupāla was slain by Kṛṣṇa;
you have stated that there is no life-force existing separate from the body. (51*)
It is said that the stainless *jīva* goes from one body to another;
yet you have stated that there is no *jīva* existing as something separate from the body. (52)
O Lord, you have described an auspicious destiny for one who dies in battle while full of wrath, yet with a mind in that very same state, you have described a miserable rebirth. (53)
The merit of the sons of Pāṇḍu has been described individually through their glorification;
those who approach women who should not be approached are censurable according to your teaching. (54)
The Skandas, Upendras, Rudras, and others always carry weapons, whether out of fear or for the purpose of terrifying; you, however, are fearless and not terrifying.
You do not frighten anyone, nor have you been frightened by anyone;
for you alone have laid down your weapons, and thus you are superior to the world.

The statements of the Vedas and other scriptures are generally contradicted by what precedes and follows; they proclaim the affliction of their speaker, whereas your word proclaims your omniscience. (57)
Other scriptures are for the most part contradictory from beginning to end; but your stainless doctrine is consistent in its beginning, middle, and conclusion.
"It has been stated by those who proclaim the Dharma that one should not impart wisdom to a Śūdra;
yet you have taught the True Dharma even to the Caṇḍālas out of compassion. (59)
Having abandoned the auspicious tree, who would practice in a thicket of evil trees?
Having encountered you, who are free from passion, what wise person would bow to other teachers? (60)
"Even while enjoying sense objects, the followers of Kapila are liberated through knowledge.
O one free from defilement, how can there be liberation for one who is afflicted, as you have stated? (61)
That which has been taught by you, O Blessed One, is not stated in other treatises:
that having accumulated a store of merit, it is dedicated for the sake of sentient beings. (62)
Having caused injury to living beings at sacrifices to the gods and shrines, worldly people desire [such] dharma; yet that has been censured by you in the scripture. (63)
How can there be Dharma in that place where the slaughter of living beings is certain?
O Lord, you have protected sentient beings even at the cost of your own life.
In which truth, non-violence, celibacy, self-restraint, and compassion—the true Dharma originating from the royal Śākya clan—are held in high esteem by you. (65)

"Even toward an assassin approaching on the battlefield, even if he is a master of the Vedanta—you have said, and you yourself have declared, that compassion extends even toward those who would kill. (66)
Your own maternal uncle was pierced by the prince with a spear;
O Hero, the net of afflictions has been torn asunder by you through the power of wisdom.
Indeed, even his own inner apartments were not protected by Viṣṇu;
yet you, O Lord, are ever intent upon protecting all sentient beings.
Knowing the fear of Jarāsaṃdha, Hari abandoned Mathurā;
O sage, there is no such being as he from whom you should be afraid. 69.
The kinsmen of Vāsudeva have gone to destruction through misconduct;
but by you, all your kinsmen have been liberated from the cycle of worldly existence.
The more I examine the doctrines of the outsiders, O Lord, the more my mind finds serene confidence in you alone. (71)

Thus, those of dull intellect, whose intentions are gripped by the perception of faults in the doctrine that [the Buddha] is not omniscient, do not perceive you, the Teacher, even though you are faultless. (72)
The world said, "These Śākyas are haters of the Vedas, the gods, and the twice-born.
But does the world not realize that this is merely its own fault? (73)
Since happiness is obtained through happiness alone in your teaching,
therefore, O tiger among debaters, these people delight in your doctrine.
By whatever merit I possess from thus proclaiming your virtues according to this rite, may the world become equal to you through that.
Whatever merit has been acquired by me through reciting this *Viśeṣastava*, by that, O Lord, may the entire world be intent upon awakening. (76)
Thus ends the *Viśeṣastava* by Bhaṭṭa Rādhāsvāmin.
